ſuperſtitious Ceremonies about Imagery and other Relicts of xeltgien

.rooted out of his Empire , baprizing himſelf , and caufing all his cover- F

and Conformity with the Primitive Church,which they fay is ſtill rhe Rudi.

' The Church of Moſcovis has like that of Rome , one ſupreme Head , 
who is the Patriarch. Under the Patriarch are 4 Metropolitans , 4, 
Arch-Biſhops, beſides many other Biſhops, Abbots and the Inferior 
Clergy. The Patriarch is almoſt Sovereign in Spiritual Aﬀairs,having 
an ablolute and immediate power without any appencency on the 
Temporal Government unlels it be in caſeof inducing Hereſy , upon 
which he muſt Submit to a Synod , as 1n the year 1662, a General 


Council was called , and: the Patriarch ſummoned to make his ap- 


pearance; at what time he was impeached for Innovations , and 1n- 
devouring toalienate the preſent condition of the Churchand reform 
it's Government by diminiſhing Image-worſhip , which he held for 
litle better than Idolatry. After many days ſitting that Council 
thought fit to confine him to his Manſion-Houſe , and ordain the 
Firſt Metropolitan in his room, who was then living when I was at 
Meſeou. The Revenues of the Patriarch, as alſo of the Metropolitans, 
are verygreat, out of which they are obliged to levy and Maintain 
an Army of 15000 men, during the time of War. 

The Habit of the Patriarch, and the Metropolitans differ but litle. 
The Patriarch has always a great Crofier born before him , or a litle 
onein his hand and ſometimes both , this they call a Poſot. Mitres 
they wear only upon Convocations or high Aiſemblies , and upon 
ſolemn Occaſions. Abroad they are diſtinguiſhed by a high Cap, 
flat at top like the Swirzers , or Yeomen of the Guard. Next their 
Bodiethey wear a Caſloc, and above that a long Gown or rather a 
Pall, which is born up by two Gentlemen. The Inferior Clergy and 
Prieſts wear a Cap but not ſo high as that of the Superiors. This Cap is 
given them when they are ordained by the Biſhops , at what time 
they ſhave their Heads, and ſuffer it to grow no more, ſave in two litle 
tufts juſt above their ears. 

There is a Law among them that whoſoever beats one of thoſe 
Clerks ſo,that his cap fall to the ground, he is liable toa very ſevere pe- 
nalty ( if I well remember to looſe his hand ) which nevertheleſs 
happens frequently in the Cabac : but to prevent the worſt when a Lay- 
man 1s minded to beat one of thoſe Muſhrooms, he firſt takes off his 
Cap and then trounces him off ſo long as hewill , which done he ſcts 
the Cap upon the right Block again.

The Clergy are not forbidden Marriage, nor none that ſerve at the ».42. 
Altar, but on thecontrary are obliged to marry, and thatonly once, 1712; 
gathering that from the Saying of S. Paul. A Bichop ought to be the Marriage 
Husband of one Wife. Nor is it lawfull for him to marry a Widow. If a > fo 
Prieſts wife come to die before him, he is not only injoyned by the © 
Church to remain a Widdower, butallſo toleavethe Altar , yer not 
wholly to lay down the Prieſtly Fun&ion, for he may ſit in the Chore 
or Chauntry and aſſiſt at Mattins and Veſpers , as alſo at Admini- 
{tration of the Sacraments, as far as it is done without the Verge of 
the Altar. For this reaſon the Prieſts are beſt matched , as uſually 
making much of their Wives , and treating them more gently than 
the Laity generally do', leſt by hard uſage they ſhould drive them 
into melancholy, and conſequently ſend them too early out of the 
World, which ſends them as ſuddenly from the Altar. 

Baptiſm they hold forth as a Sacrament very neceſſary , for which of np 
reaſon they make as litle delay as may be between the Womb and the ©* 
Font. If they fear the Child be wok they have it Baptized at home, 
but never in the ſame Room where it is born, for that they hold un- 
clean. The Conſponſors or God-fathers being come to the Church 
Porch , the Prieſt meets them and repeats the Benediftion. The 
Godfathers deliver 9 Wax-candles to the Prieſt , which he places 
round about the Font afterwards turning about toward the Eaſt 
mutters outa Verſicleor two, then taking the Incens-pan goes round 
aboutthe Font , which done he ſings a Pfalm or Hymn , making a 
brief Oraizon, and after that demands the name of the Infant which 
is delivered him in writing. So ſoon as he has read the Billet , askes, 
whether the Child beleeves in the Sacred Trinity ? and , Whether 
he utterly Forſake the Devil, &c. To which they confidently reply 
in the Affirmative. Then the Prieſt pronounces this Adjuration, Get 
thee hence, than untlean Spirit , and make way for the Holy Ghoſt, Then he 
takes the child into his Arms, blowing three times in his Face , and 
making a croſs upon his Head, dips it three times in Water, Saying, 
Tbaptize theein the Nameofthe FATHER , andofthe SON , andofthe
